text.p: Vimpel-Communications, the largest cellular telecommunications provider in Russia, said on Tuesday it filed a registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for its planned American Depository Share offering.
The company said in a statement it planned to offer depositary shares representing about 3.92 million common shares in the United States, Canada and elsewhere.
The company also said it would apply to list the ADSs on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol VIP.N.
Vimpel markets it services under the brand name "Bee Line," and said it operates primarily in the Moscow area, covering a population of 15 million.
Vimpel said it would do a concurrent combined offering, in the United States and Canada, and another outside that area.
According to published reports, Vimpel had a 59 percent market share in the Moscow license area, it said.

It operates the only Digital Advanced Mobile Phone System (AMPS) 800 MHz cellular system there, it said. It said it is the only company to be granted a personal communications services license in that area.
Vimpel said it also has licenses to operate AMPS networks in six other Russian regions -- Samara, Tver, Vladimir, Novgorod, Ryazan and the Leningrad Region, not including the city of St. Petersburg.
The global coordinators of the offerings are Renaissance Capital Group and Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corporation, it said.
